The cost of deciding whether a permutation mixes

Suppose an input circuit computes a permutation PP of nn-bit strings. Deciding whether its XOR-difference chain converges to uniform from every nonzero starting difference is NP-hard, even when an inverse circuit is also supplied. With an explicit table, the graph can be built in O(22n)O(2^{2n}) table lookups, polynomial in the table length. A circuit can describe the same table much more compactly.

Reduction from satisfiability

Given a Boolean formula FF on mm variables, use n=m+3n=m+3 bits x=(x0,x1,x2,y)x=(x_0,x_1,x_2,y), where yy has mm bits. Let RR rotate the nn coordinates one place to the left. Define f(x)=1f(x)=1 exactly when x1=x2=0x_1=x_2=0 and F(y)=1F(y)=1. Let e0e_0 be the first unit vector and set

H(x)=x⊕f(x)e0,P(x)=R(H(x)). H(x)=x\oplus f(x)e_0,\qquad P(x)=R(H(x)).

The function ff ignores x0x_0, so HH is its own inverse. Both PP and P−1=H∘R−1P^{-1}=H\circ R^{-1} have circuit size O(|F|+n)O(|F|+n). If FF is unsatisfiable, P=RP=R. Every difference then rotates deterministically, preserving its Hamming weight. The chain is disconnected.

Suppose FF is satisfiable. The difference graph contains an edge a→ba\to b whenever some xx satisfies P(x)⊕P(x⊕a)=bP(x)\oplus P(x\oplus a)=b. Two kinds of edges suffice.

  1. Rotation. For every a≠0a\ne0, some xx has f(x)=f(x⊕a)=0f(x)=f(x\oplus a)=0. The support of ff and its translate each cover at most a quarter of the domain. This gives the edge a→Raa\to Ra.
  2. Flip followed by rotation. When a1=1a_1=1, take xx with x1=x2=0x_1=x_2=0 and yy a satisfying assignment. Then f(x)=1f(x)=1 and f(x⊕a)=0f(x\oplus a)=0, giving a→R(a⊕e0)a\to R(a\oplus e_0).

Follow the second edge with n−1n-1 rotation edges. This gives a path that toggles bit 0 whenever bit 1 is set. Rotating before and after this path lets any set bit toggle its predecessor, with indices taken cyclically. Starting at a set bit of any nonzero difference, walk backwards around the cycle and turn each zero encountered into a one. Thus every state can reach the all-ones state. Each toggle leaves its controlling bit set, so each path of toggles can be undone. The graph is strongly connected. Rotation fixes the all-ones state, giving a self-loop and hence period one.

The chain is doubly stochastic because PP permutes ordered pairs of distinct inputs. Strong connectivity and period one therefore give convergence to uniform. We have a polynomial-time many-one reduction taking satisfiable formulas exactly to mixing permutations. Cook's satisfiability theorem

Exact query bound for a black-box permutation

For n≥3n\ge3, a deterministic exact tester needs 2n−12^n-1 evaluations in the worst case. Set q=2nq=2^n. Over the field of order qq, multiplication by a generator of the multiplicative group gives a linear map LL that cycles all q−1q-1 nonzero differences. Its chain is periodic. Swapping any two outputs of LL makes it mix, as follows.

Write the modified permutation as P=τ∘LP=\tau\circ L, where the transposition τ\tau exchanges two points differing by δ≠0\delta\ne0. For an input difference aa, the two points before τ\tau differ by LaLa. At most four choices of the first point touch either swapped point, so every edge a→Laa\to La survives. When La≠δLa\ne\delta, choosing the first point to be a swapped point changes the difference by δ\delta. The graph therefore also contains a→La⊕δa\to La\oplus\delta. The map I+LI+L is invertible because LL fixes no nonzero point. Taking a=(I+L)−1δa=(I+L)^{-1}\delta gives a self-loop from this second edge, since a≠0a\ne0 and La≠δLa\ne\delta. The surviving cycle and this self-loop prove mixing.

On the oracle LL, any two unqueried inputs could still have their outputs swapped. An exact tester must query all but one input, and the permutation promise then determines the last output. Bounded-error randomized testers also require Ω(q)\Omega(q) queries. Couple the oracle LL to a copy with a uniformly random pair swapped. Until a query hits that pair the two transcripts coincide, and the probability of a hit in kk queries is at most 2k/q2k/q.

In particular, a two-answer tester with worst-case error ε<1/2\varepsilon<1/2 must have 2k/q≥1−2ε2k/q\ge1-2\varepsilon. The two inputs need to produce different answers with probability at least 1−2ε1-2\varepsilon. This bound holds even if the queries are evaluated in parallel. It concerns point evaluations. A known circuit exposes additional structure to a proof.

Screening for invariant parities

Large permutations are often supplied as an algorithm, Boolean circuit or callable that computes one image at a time. For example, fixing an AES key specifies a permutation on 128-bit blocks, compactly represented by its round transformations and key schedule. A public unkeyed design such as the 320-bit Ascon permutation is also specified by layers of operations on words. In the pairwise experiment the chosen permutation is fixed across rounds, while the experiment supplies fresh common XOR keys. NIST AES standard · Ascon designers' permutation specification

For n≥2n\ge2, seek a nonzero mask mm such that

m⋅P(x)=m⋅x⊕m⋅P(0)for all x,m\cdot P(x)=m\cdot x\ \oplus\ m\cdot P(0)\quad\text{for all }x,

where the dot product is binary parity. Such a mask preserves the parity of every difference through every round. The nonzero differences with m⋅a=0m\cdot a=0 form a nonempty proper closed set, proving disconnection. Define v(x)=P(x)⊕x⊕P(0)v(x)=P(x)\oplus x\oplus P(0). The allowed masks form the orthogonal complement of the span of the v(x)v(x). Binary elimination therefore finds all invariant hyperplanes in one table scan using O(nN)O(nN) word operations in total and O(n)O(n) words for the basis (each nn bits). Full rank rules out every such mask immediately. The six-bit block-swap example shows that other obstructions can remain. Implementation · Six-bit counterexample

On a callable, use the same elimination on kk independent uniform nonzero inputs and the anchor P(0)P(0). For a mask whose equation fails on at least a δ\delta fraction of all inputs, the chance of passing is at most (1−δ)k(1-\delta)^k. Zero always satisfies the equation, so sampling nonzero inputs only improves the bound. A union bound over all nonzero masks gives at most (2n−1)e−kδ(2^n-1)e^{-k\delta} for any such mask to survive. Thus k≥(nln2+ln(1/ε))/δk\ge(n\ln2+\ln(1/\varepsilon))/\delta suffices, and genuine invariant masks survive every sample. A surviving candidate can have rare exceptions. This error bound concerns the parity identity. The general black-box lower bound above applies to deciding mixing itself.

Given a circuit and a candidate mm, ask a Boolean satisfiability solver whether there exists an xx with m⋅v(x)=1m\cdot v(x)=1. A satisfying assignment discards the candidate and an unsatisfiability proof certifies nonmixing. One can similarly verify a proposed proper subspace WW with basis wiw_i. Search for x,ix,i with P(x)⊕P(x⊕wi)∉WP(x)\oplus P(x\oplus w_i)\notin W. If the formula is unsatisfiable, telescoping the basis shifts proves closure for every w∈Ww\in W. Solver runtime depends on the circuit. The Python screen implements the elimination and sampling steps.
